title: Sunday · the empty town
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · the aggregator
logline: Spring. No tourists. No lockbox turnover. Main street with nobody in it. The strip doesn't say why.

panels.composition: Tier 1: main street, April, wet-on-wet. Empty. Every lockbox closed. Every laminated card gone from the windows. A single figure and a dog in the middle of the road.

image.prompt: a small coastal main street in April, completely empty, key lockboxes closed on every door, no cards in the windows, one man and a small three-legged dog standing in the middle of the road, wet-on-wet watercolor, no words
image.notes: Reserved whether 2020 is 2020. The strip shows only the emptiness.

panels.name: Empty

panels.composition: Tier 2: Gully's. The chalkboard turned to the wall. A hand-lettered sign in the door: WINDOW ONLY. Gully's shape inside. One cup on the sill.

image.prompt: a shingle bait-and-espresso shack with a hand-lettered WINDOW ONLY sign in its door and a chalkboard turned to the wall, a man's shape inside, a single paper cup set on the window sill, watercolor

panels.name: Window only

panels.composition: Tier 3: the beach. Empty. The drift log. The two of them on it. The whole town's beach with nobody on it but them, which is how it was in 1999.

image.prompt: an empty gray beach with a man and a three-legged dog on a bleached drift log, nobody else anywhere, watercolor, no words

panels.name: Theirs again

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; Sundays wet-on-wet; 2019: the Sunday drawn to a smaller grid
art.palette: ink and one tone; Sundays gray-green, fog, rust; 2020: ochre and slate arriving

notes: The empty town. Why is never said. The beach is theirs again.
